She gave us an exam on Spring break. She scheduled class hours during the weekend. These times should be reserved for students, but rather than respecting the rights of students and using make-up hours (that are there to be used for exams, extra class hours) she carelessly takes away these rights from us. When one student emailed Michelle Hoca about the exam in Spring break, she sent a message to the Whatsapp group (where most students in the course had joined in) as such: "I have received an e-mail from Michelle Hoca, saying that she and the Dean received emails about the midterm we will have on this Sunday...First of all, you could have discussed me earlier...Secondly, I cannot understand why you prefer to contact directly with Michelle Hoca and the Dean, without discussing this with me first. You are always welcome to discuss anything." Not only is she trying to keep us silent, but she is also trying to take away our right to notify the department administration about her behavior. She is also being hypocritical because when she scheduled the second midterm on the 26th of April from 7-9 P.M. a number of students asked if she could reschedule since it was Ramadan and they were going to be fasting during the day. She made these students take the exam at 7 P.M. when they had not eaten for at least 15 hours. Her reason was that she was busy. She discriminated against all of the students that were fasting. After students had expressed concern for the exam scheduling, she sent this email: "First of all, I would like to say that I am really bothered of all of the discussions going on this semester...Sometimes, the circumstances may not make you happy." 
Thus;
1) She is egocentric and only cares about herself and her needs. 
2) She has no regard for the mental health of the students in her class. 
3) She abuses her power over us and expects us to conform to everything she subjects us to.
4) She does not respect the boundaries of students.

This is the most flawed course I've ever taken in my undergraduate career so far. First, the majority of the topics it includes are either psychoanalytic/neo-psychoanalytic in nature, thus making the majority of the course being closer to philosophy than actual psychology that is based on the scientific method, what is even sadder is the fact that we do not even touch upon the relevant and most used personality theories nowadays (e.g. the big 5). Secondly, the textbook used is the most superficial textbook I've ever encountered, it does not go in detail with the explanations and what makes it even worse is that the exams expect us to have a detailed knowledge about the topics, these two combined was a recipe for disaster. Moreover, this course takes way more time than it should be given, from 5 pop quizzes to 2 midterms and a final to a project to strict attendance policy...

The instructor is unable to explain some parts of the theories, which makes us doubt whether she has sufficient knowledge on the topics. The course focus is mostly on theories and the personal lives of the theorists. We spend at least a whole hour on the personal lives of course theorists (for each theorist) which is unnecessary. Instead, we should be focusing on the parts of the personality theories that are empirically supported so we are not left with useless information. Yet unfortunately this is not the case.
